Combat: Attacks and Defenses

Combat uses attack rolls and defense rolls. An attack roll is a task to determine whether an attack succeeds. Defense rolls determine whether you avoid, block, or otherwise resist an attack or effect.

You can always choose to not defend against an attack, in which case it automatically hits you.

Some effects and NPC attacks might bypass blocks and dodges. For example, a trap that releases poison gas might have you make a Might defense roll, and a mental blast from a psychic monster might have you make an Intellect defense roll.

Sometimes an attack provokes two defense actions. For example, a venomous snake might require a block or dodge followed by a Might defense roll against its poison.

If a defense roll fails, some attacks may confer an ongoing hostile effect that requires you to use a recovery to end it. If you use a recovery this way, you don’t get the benefits a recovery normally grants.

Armor and Shields

Armor indicates how much less damage a character takes from an attack. Shields protect against attacks when a block roll succeeds: instead of reducing the wound’s severity by one step, the shield can take the entire wound so the character takes no damage.
